title: Political campaigns are using AI to hold personalised text conversations at scale
friendlyTitle: Political campaign texts are becoming AI conversations
summary: NPR reports that campaign platforms are training bots to answer voter questions in a candidate’s voice, continue text conversations and collect signals about individual concerns. Providers describe rapid adoption, while critics question whether the technology improves outreach or simply makes political messaging more persistent.
friendlySummary: Some campaigns now use AI bots to answer questions and keep personalised text conversations going with many voters at once.
whyItMatters: A political text may now be an adaptive conversation rather than a fixed message from a volunteer. Recipients should know they may be speaking to software and be cautious about sharing personal views or information in an unverified exchange.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The person texting you may actually be software that learns from your answers. Check who sent the message and be careful about sharing personal information.
